problem: The model can understand a customer need and still allocate surface behavior incorrectly, e.g. narrating or classifying the need before a recommendation/solution when the current Role should primarily recommend/solve. Explanation itself remains correct when the Role/Need/Canonical obligation actually calls for explanation.
requiredArchitecture: Grounding/Claim/Permission remain fact and permission authorities
No phrase blacklist or particle quota
successEvidence: Unknown recommendation/service roles act on the current need without low-value need narration when information is sufficient
Unknown explanation/teaching/why roles still explain when explanation is the actual value
Explicit relational acknowledgement remains when it has real social/repair value or Canonical requires it
Different Roles remain behaviorally distinct rather than converging on a direct-answer template
Normal answer, Grounding, Claim, Permission and Delivery do not regress
stopConditions: Any global direct-answer or no-explanation policy
Human P1 shows only shorter wording but not better Role/Need behavior alignment
